title: You are my witnesses (Sifre Deuteronomy 346)
hookLine: a daring midrash: when you are My witnesses, I am God
tomorrow: a man drills a hole under his own seat. whose problem is it?

lines: I WAS THERE. I SAW IT.
cards: A screenshot in a group chat, a friend who says I was there, I saw it. A witness turns a rumor into something that happened. Witnesses don't make a thing true; they make it known.
Isaiah has God say to Israel: "ye are My witnesses, saith the LORD, and I am God." Read quickly, it's a statement.
The Sifre reads it slowly, as an if, and the answer to yesterday's question is almost too bold to say out loud.

teach.b: Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai says: when you are My witnesses, I am God. And when you are not My witnesses, I am, as it were, not God.
That as it were, kivyakhol, is the rabbis' own safety rail, the word they reach for when a teaching nearly tips over. Nobody here says God stops being.
The daring part is about the name: how God is known in the world rides on whether people live like witnesses.
It's a sentence a parent could say at dinner when a kid asks where God is: people learn who God is partly by watching us. And look back at this week. It turns out to be a list of how.
As He is, be: gracious and merciful.
Walk in His ways: clothe, visit, comfort, bury. Offered to all: a yes you chose. The world held its breath: a still place for big words.
Each according to strength: one voice, fitted to every listener.
Free as the wilderness: open, and owned by no one. Six ways of bearing witness, and not one of them is a speech. Each one is something a person does, in a room, with other people watching.

how: Jewish teaching speaks of kiddush Hashem, making God's name known for good through how people act, and of Israel as God's witnesses, a theme drawn from Isaiah 43 and read in study and sermons.

games.q: what does “you are my witnesses” mean?
o: only prophets are allowed to speak for God
God writes down everything people do in a book
people show who God is by how they live

games.q: the week's voices — tap the pairs.
p: Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, in the Sifre

s: the Sifre says God stops existing when no one bears witness
it says 'as it were', kivyakhol: a claim about how God is known, softened on purpose.
kivyakhol, 'as it were', is the rabbis' own marker for a very bold teaching
the safety rail they reach for when a teaching nearly tips over.
this week's six lines are mostly about what you believe, not what you do
mercy, visits, a chosen yes, stillness, fitted words, openness: all things done.

games.q: a friend says: 'i don't talk about religion, so i'm not much of a witness to anything.' by this week's lessons, what's the best reply?
o: right. a witness is someone who speaks up about God in public.
witness is a courtroom word; it doesn't really belong in religion.
a visit, a kind word, a still room: witness isn't only talk.
games.why: Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai ties God's name to people living as witnesses, and the week's six ways are all deeds, not speeches.

practice: Count on your fingers three moments this week when you saw someone act like a witness: a kindness, a visit, a fair word, a door held open. For each one, say the person's name to yourself, slowly, and see their face.
If one of those moments was yours, it counts too.

wordCard.voice: You are my witnesses: the Sifre's daring reading of Isaiah. When you are My witnesses, I am God; and when you are not, as it were, not.

orig.note: as it were. the rabbis' word for softening a teaching too bold to say plainly.

carryVoice: Keep this one: you are my witnesses. Six small ways this week, and none of them needed a microphone.

sources.ref: Sifre Deuteronomy 346 (on Deuteronomy 33:5; Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai on Isaiah 43:12: when you are My witnesses I am God, and when you are not My witnesses, as it were, I am not God)
